sections.answer: General (under honorable conditions) discharges and entry-level separations
sections.components:
- c1: General (under honorable conditions) discharges
- c2: entry-level separations
sections.evidence:
- D05 (32 CFR part 73 definitions, "Characterization of less than honorable", L428) [c1, c2]: "A characterization that is less than honorable includes a general under honorable conditions, other than honorable conditions, uncharacterized, bad-conduct discharge, dishonorable discharge, or a dismissal."
- D05 (definitions, "Characterization of a discharge or dismissal", L427) [c2]: "or can be described as uncharacterized (as in an entry-level separation)"
- D03 (amended regulation, paragraph (a) General rule, L383) [c1]: "A discharge under honorable conditions is binding on the Department of Veterans Affairs as to character of discharge."
- D03 (preamble, Willful and Persistent Misconduct, B. Minor Misconduct, L210) [c1]: "If a SM has an Honorable or General discharge, VA does not conduct a COD determination"
- D03 (section IV, Uncharacterized Discharges, L277) [c2]: "there are three types of uncharacterized separations: (1) entry level separation; (2) void enlistment or induction; and (3) dropped from the rolls."
- D03 (section IV, L277) [c2]: "An entry level separation is considered under conditions other than dishonorable"
- D03 (section IV, L277) [c2]: "Void enlistments are reviewed under the factors listed in 38 CFR 3.14"
- D03 (section IV, L278) [c2]: "the facts and circumstances surrounding the separation must be reviewed to determine whether the separation was under conditions other than dishonorable"

sections.lever checks:
- Family and target: match then exclude across two documents with a late member: Doc 5 defines the Discharge Appeal Review Board's "less than honorable" set; Doc 3 states which separations VA accepts as other than dishonorable without a character-of-discharge review. Found by independent author B (b01, origin claude), wording refined by the caller (sketch i01). Target medium (user 2026-10-09: no Easy slot, "target medium and high"). Platform quick test of this exact wording and answer (user report 2026-10-09, "i01 survived, others failed"): survived; rev 0 adopts it word for word. A quick-test survival is a first screen, not a tier: aq-02483 q02 survived its quick test and then measured Too easy (Low 5/5). Difficulty result pending.
- Dependency plan: Doc 5 L428 (candidate set: general, OTH, uncharacterized, BCD, dishonorable, dismissal) and L427 (uncharacterized "as in an entry-level separation"; court-martial characterizations) -> Doc 3 L383 and L210 (general binding, no COD determination) -> Doc 3 L277-279 (three uncharacterized types; only entry level considered other than dishonorable; void enlistments and dropped-from-the-rolls reviewed) -> Doc 3 L117, L68, L244, L52 (OTH assessed, BCD/OTH case by case, dishonorable excluded, GCM discharge or dismissal a statutory bar) -> answer {general (under honorable conditions) discharges, entry-level separations}.
- Universe: Doc 5's six less-than-honorable kinds, with uncharacterized split by Doc 3 into three types = eight candidates. In: general (Doc 3 L383, L210); entry level separation (L277). Out: OTH (L117: "each OTH discharge is assessed"), void enlistment (L277: "reviewed under the factors listed in 38 CFR 3.14"), dropped from the rolls (L278-279: "must be reviewed ... in the same manner as if such former SM received an OTH discharge"), BCD (L68: case-by-case analysis; a GCM sentence is a statutory bar, L52 and L390), dishonorable (L244: "excluded from benefits eligibility"), dismissal (Doc 5 L427: assigned at court-martial; Doc 3 L52: "discharged or dismissed by GCM" barred since 1944; Doc 3 L282 lists Coast Guard officer "dismissal pursuant to GCM or administrative separation" with no VA acceptance statement). Honorable is accepted (L383) but fails "less than honorable" (Doc 5 L428).
- Necessity: Doc 5 is the only document defining the board's less-than-honorable set (grep "less than honorable": D05 only; Doc 3 never mentions the board) and the only one placing general and uncharacterized/entry-level separations in it; without Doc 5 the candidate set, and general's counter-intuitive membership, is unknown. Doc 3 is the only document stating VA's treatment of general, entry-level, void, dropped, OTH, BCD and dishonorable separations (grep "entry level", "binding", "COD determination": D03 only); Doc 5's VA remarks (L329 GI Bill honorable only; L332 OTH "fact-specific basis") cover neither general nor entry-level acceptance and would mislead. Docs 1, 2, 4, 6 and 7 hold none of these terms. Both remain needed after wording; the question names neither answer item.
- Selected-lever checks: Match, then exclude: without Doc 3's filter the answer would be all six Doc 5 kinds (general, OTH, uncharacterized, BCD, dishonorable, dismissal), so the exclusion changes the answer. Bury one list item late: entry level separation appears only in Doc 3's section IV (character offset about 72,400 of 92,900) and in Doc 5's parenthetical (L427), not in Doc 5's list itself, which says "uncharacterized". Decoy check: "uncharacterized" as a block fails for void enlistments and dropped-from-the-rolls separations (L277-279).
- Targeted failure modes: mode 1 (Part vs total / Wrong members in a list): taking the whole uncharacterized category (Doc 5 L428, equated with entry-level at L427) -> "general and uncharacterized separations", too broad per Doc 3 L277-279. Mode 2 (Wrong jurisdiction or scope / Misapplies a rule or premise): applying the GI Bill's honorable-only education rule (Doc 5 L329 "even separation under general (under honorable conditions) does not qualify"; Doc 3 L82) to VA's character-of-discharge standard -> "entry-level separations" only; Doc 3 L383 binds general discharges for character of discharge. Mode 3 (Linking across documents / Wrong members in a list): not tying Doc 5's "uncharacterized" to Doc 3's section IV -> "general (under honorable conditions) discharges" only. All three wrong answers recomputed from the cited lines (caller, 2026-10-09). No platform attempts observed yet. Considered and not declared: honorable included (fails "less than honorable", wording rules it out); OTH included because VA deems OTH eligible "more than 75%" of the time (Doc 3 L118-122: a determination outcome, not automatic acceptance; plausible but weaker).
- Calculation verification: not applicable (membership list). Universe enumeration checked by reading every characterization in Doc 5 L427-428 and Doc 3 L50-53, L68, L117, L210, L244, L277-283, L383-401.
- Semantic/ID/overview probes: grep across D01-D07 for "less than honorable", "uncharacterized", "entry level"/"entry-level", "general (under honorable", "binding", "COD determination": hits only in D03 and D05. No passage pairs the board's scope with VA's acceptance or states the two-item answer. Overview: Doc 5's summary says the board reviews "requests to upgrade a service member's discharge characterization"; Doc 3's summary mentions bars and the compelling circumstances exception; neither names general discharges or entry-level separations. Shortest route: Doc 5 L428 -> Doc 3 L210/L383 for general -> Doc 3 section IV (L277) for uncharacterized.
- Precision/readings: "automatically accept as other than dishonorable" paraphrases "binding ... as to character of discharge" (general) and "is considered under conditions other than dishonorable" (entry level); void enlistments and dropped-from-the-rolls separations are "reviewed", OTH "assessed", BCD "case-by-case", so none is automatic. "Separations" covers discharges and separations alike. Grading risk: an answer of "uncharacterized" alone may be read as entry-level through Doc 5's parenthetical; the gold names entry-level separations. Answer order is free (two items joined by "and").
- Completeness: full corpus, no gaps (intake: incomplete false, gap 0 for all seven documents). Doc 3's regulatory text prints "* * * * *" for paragraphs (c)(2)-(5), (f), the conditions of (h) and parts of (i): these are elided in the published amendment itself, not capture gaps, and do not bear on acceptance of general or entry-level separations (the 1944 GCM bar is stated at L52 and L390).
- Style/set review: 21 words, one ask, wording as quick-tested. No other live question on this bundle; i02 and i03 failed the quick test (user 2026-10-09) and share no answer path with q01.
- Warnings answered: TODO after preflight.

sections.question: Which separations does DoD's Discharge Appeal Review Board count as less than honorable but VA automatically accept as other than dishonorable?
sections.reasoning:
Step 1. Source input (Doc 5, the rule's definitions, "Characterization of less than honorable"): for the Discharge Appeal Review Board, a less than honorable characterization includes a general (under honorable conditions) discharge, other than honorable (OTH) conditions, uncharacterized, a bad-conduct discharge (BCD), a dishonorable discharge and a dismissal. These are the candidates.
Step 2. Source input (Doc 5, definitions, "Characterization of a discharge or dismissal"): an administrative discharge "can be described as uncharacterized (as in an entry-level separation)", and bad-conduct discharges, dishonorable discharges and dismissals are the characterizations a court-martial assigns. So entry-level separations sit inside the uncharacterized candidate above.
Step 3. Source input (Doc 3, amended regulation, paragraph (a) General rule, and the preamble on minor misconduct): "A discharge under honorable conditions is binding on the Department of Veterans Affairs as to character of discharge", and for an Honorable or General discharge "VA does not conduct a COD determination". A general (under honorable conditions) discharge therefore meets VA's other-than-dishonorable standard automatically: keep it (component c1).
Step 4. Source input (Doc 3, section IV, Uncharacterized Discharges): VA splits uncharacterized separations into entry level separation, void enlistment or induction, and dropped from the rolls. Only the first "is considered under conditions other than dishonorable"; void enlistments are reviewed under a separate regulation, and a dropped-from-the-rolls separation "must be reviewed" the same way as an OTH discharge. Keep entry-level separations (component c2) and drop the other two uncharacterized types.
Step 5. Source input (Doc 3, preamble): each OTH discharge "is assessed to determine VA benefits eligibility"; BCD and OTH cases get "a case-by-case, more holistic analysis"; dishonorable discharges "are excluded from benefits eligibility"; and discharge or dismissal by general court-martial has been a statutory bar since the 1944 Act. None of these is accepted automatically, so OTH, BCD, dishonorable and dismissal drop out.
Step 6. Filter (Doc 5 candidates against Doc 3 treatment, combining the steps above): the less than honorable characterizations that VA accepts as other than dishonorable without a review are general (under honorable conditions) discharges and entry-level separations. An honorable discharge is also binding on VA but is not on Doc 5's less than honorable list. The GI Bill's honorable-only requirement (Doc 5, Doc 3) limits education benefits, not VA's character-of-discharge standard, so it does not remove general discharges.
Decoy: uncharacterized separations as a whole. Doc 5 lists "uncharacterized" and gives an entry-level separation as its example, but Doc 3 reviews void enlistments and dropped-from-the-rolls separations, so only the entry-level type qualifies.
Final answer: General (under honorable conditions) discharges and entry-level separations.
sections.targeted failure modes:
### Failure mode 1
Trap: Part vs total
How a careless solver fails: Wrong members in a list

### Failure mode 2
Trap: Wrong jurisdiction or scope
How a careless solver fails: Misapplies a rule or premise

### Failure mode 3
Trap: Linking across documents
How a careless solver fails: Wrong members in a list

Why these are traps: Part vs total: Doc 3 section IV accepts only the entry-level part of uncharacterized separations, so 'general and uncharacterized' is too broad. Linking: missing that part gives 'general only'. Scope: Doc 5's honorable-only GI Bill line tempts 'entry-level only', but Doc 3's general rule binds general discharges.
